source_text.body:
Run a large document review on an agent's cloud computer
The writer assigned a Dot a big document-review job on its own cloud computer and says it kept its place and continued working over time.
·
Oct 1, 2026
Done with
DO
Dots
What they did
The writer gave a Dot a document-review assignment covering hundreds of PDFs and thousands of pages, and says it ran on the Dot’s own cloud computer rather than as a short one-off run. During the multi-day review, the Dot kept its place, answered a side question by checking other materials, updated its understanding, then resumed the packet without the writer rebuilding the task.
How it went
The reported result was continuity: the review became a multi-day job that persisted through interruptions, which the writer says mattered more than speed. They do not give completion numbers or quality metrics, and they note their model is based on about a day of testing.
Worth knowing
The main catch is uncertainty around usage: the writer says they have not established how work done by the Dot, background agents, or launched tasks is counted.
Try it yourself
with
Dots
Copy prompt
I'm giving you a large document review job on your cloud computer. Review all files in [folder or link] for [what to check, e.g. missing signatures, risky clauses, inconsistencies], keep a running log of which files are done, and continue until every file is covered. Finish with one summary report of findings per document, and ask me before you edit, delete or send anything.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ChatGPT/comments/1wuzlvp/i_spent_a_day_poking_dots_with_sticks_heres_what
